title: app crashes on a fragment chain if later fragment has `run_every` and and later no longer runs
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment sits in a fragment and runs, where the later fragment has a run_every set, when an earlier fragment reruns but switches path to not run later fragment the app crashes.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


[USER].fragment
def function_1():
    if st.toggle(label=" ", value=True):
        function_2()


[USER].fragment
def function_2():
    function_3()


[USER].fragment(run_every=3)
def function_3():
    pass


function_1()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run app 
2. set toggle to off on app
3. wait for 3 seconds (or however long the run_every parameter is set to)

### Expected Behavior

App should not crash and just re-run earlier fragment without the later fragments.

### Current Behavior

App crashes and goes into a white screen, on browser console we see

```
Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path
```

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.55.0
- Python version: 3.12.8
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

Seems to work in version 1.37.0 when fragments were inrtoduced, after a while instead of crashing we get a bad message format pop up. on 1.55.0 and a few earlier versions the screen goes white

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15084)

### Triage Analysis

This is a **bug / regression** affecting nested `st.fragment` chains where an inner fragment uses `run_every`. In the repro, `function_1` (toggle) → `function_2` → `function_3 (run_every=3)`. After the user toggles off, an `function_1` fragment-rerun no longer descends into `function_2`/`function_3`, but `function_3` is still scheduled to auto-rerun via `run_every`. When that scheduled rerun fires, the frontend throws `Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path` and the app goes to a white screen.

**Likely root cause (preliminary):**

- When a fragment is run via `fragment_id_queue` (auto-rerun or widget-triggered), `_fragment_storage.clear(...)` is **not** called — that only runs in the full-app branch (`lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py` ~L709–L716). So after the toggle-off rerun of `function_1`, the inner fragments `function_2`/`function_3` remain registered in `fragment_storage` and `function_3`'s `auto_rerun` timer is still in flight.
- The rerun of `function_1` re-creates its child container, so the delta-path coordinates that `function_3` originally captured (relative to its enclosing container/fragment cursor in `lib/streamlit/runtime/fragment.py` ~L226–L231) no longer point at a valid block in the new tree.
- When `function_3`'s auto-rerun then sends a delta, `SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor` walks the path and hits the `if (!node.children[currentIndex])` + `remainingPath.length > 0` branch, raising `"Cannot set a node at a delta path"` (`frontend/lib/src/render-tree/visitors/SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor.ts` L123–L126), which is the exact error reported.

In other words, an inner fragment whose ancestor was not re-executed on the latest run becomes "orphaned" but continues to emit periodic deltas at a stale path. The fix likely needs to either (a) prevent orphaned descendant fragments from auto-rerunning when an ancestor fragment ran without re-registering them, or (b) make the frontend gracefully drop deltas pointing into a missing sub-tree (instead of crashing).

The reporter notes 1.37.0 just worked, while a few recent versions show "bad message format" before transitioning to the white-screen crash on 1.55.0 — consistent with this being a regression in the fragment lifecycle handling.

### Related Issues

- [#10719 – Nested periodic st.fragments can cause StreamlitDuplicateElementId](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10719) — Same area (nested fragments + `run_every`) and very similar lifecycle/ordering pitfalls; likely shares root cause around how nested fragments and their delta paths/IDs are reconciled across reruns.
- [#11971 – SelectboxColumn in data editor not working when fragment with run_every is active](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11971) — Another `run_every` fragment side-effect bug where periodic reruns disturb sibling tree state, suggesting general issues with how `run_every` deltas interact with the rest of the tree.
- [#12514 – Fragments within container disappearing on rerender](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12514) — Also about nested fragments inside containers losing/corrupting their tree state on subsequent renders, which is the same family of "fragment + container delta path" reconciliation problems.
